clue.text: Tribe to acquire a mechanical contrivance

parts.note: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel
to acquire something is to get it

explanation.surface: A tribe sets out to obtain some piece of machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget is a small ingenious device or piece of equipment.

clue.text: A quad tree possibly non-existent — right? Good enough

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters left over may be put in another order
non-existent tells us the letter for right is absent from the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an imaginary quad tree would be satisfactory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-existent' removes R (right) from A QUAD TREE, leaving AQUADTEE, which 'possibly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate describes something sufficient or satisfactory, no more.

clue.text: Shape of Shakespearian theatre in the round?

definitions.text: Shape of Shakespearian theatre in the round?

parts.words: Shape of Shakespearian theatre in the round?
parts.note: Shakespeare's theatre was the Globe, and a globe is round, so its shape would be globe-like, i.e. spherical

explanation.surface: A question about the layout of an Elizabethan playhouse staged in the round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the round' is theatre jargon for a central stage, but here it means spherical; the Globe was Shakespeare's playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Globular means shaped like a ball or sphere.

clue.text: An eight-footer, thanks to natural evolution

parts.note: ta is an informal British word for thanks

indicators.note: evolution suggests gradual change, so the word natural develops into a new order

explanation.surface: A creature with eight feet owes its form to natural evolution.
explanation.definitionFit: This large hairy spider has eight legs, so it is jokingly an eight-footer.

clue.text: Where uncle is wrong describing chess moves

definitions.meaning: 'uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, whose place of business this is
split as two words this says chess pieces hop, a false account of how the smallest pieces move

explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker. Split the answer as PAWNS HOP and it is a wrong description of chess moves, since pawns step rather than hop.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawnbroker lends money against goods at his shop, so that is where 'uncle' is found.

clue.text: Creator of optical, illusion, they say

definitions.text: Creator of optical, illusion, they say

parts.words: Creator of optical, illusion, they say
parts.note: a conjuror is said to deceive the eye with sleight of hand, producing illusions

explanation.surface: Someone is reputed to be the maker of an optical illusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror performing sleight of hand fools the eye, which is what this long word names.

clue.text: No charge for so small a matter?

definitions.text: No charge for so small a matter?

parts.words: No charge for so small a matter?
parts.note: reads like a trader waiving a fee for a trifle, but describes a tiny particle of matter with no electric charge

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper waives payment because the item is so trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle in the nucleus carries no electric charge.

clue.text: French company taken in hand on a plantation

indicators.note: taken in means one piece is held inside another

parts.note: taken as written
Cie is the French abbreviation for compagnie, company

explanation.surface: A French firm is taken in hand while working on a plantation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' puts CIE inside HAND; A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate or plantation in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Unwelcome cause of deflation

parts.note: sounds economic, but describes a hole letting the air out of a tyre

explanation.surface: An economist bemoans whatever is pushing prices down.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat tyre is caused by a small hole letting the air escape.

clue.text: Right to payment concerning lecture series

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a course is a series of lectures

explanation.surface: A lecturer claims a right to be paid for a series of talks.
explanation.definitionFit: In law and finance this is the right to demand payment, for example from the drawer of a bill.

clue.text: Classic forger of pointless clue back in front

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the van is the front of an army or procession

indicators.note: back tells us the shortened word is read in the opposite direction
pointless removes a compass point, here the east

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old counterfeiter's pointless clue is pinned up at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR read 'clue' as 'due'. 'pointless' removes E from CLUE, 'back' turns CLU to ULC, and 'in' puts that inside VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulcan was the Roman god of fire and the smith who forged at his anvil.

clue.text: French refugee, oddly enough, but beheaded

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters are arranged in a strange new way
beheaded removes the first letter of the word but

explanation.surface: A French refugee, curiously, but without a head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' turns BUT into UT; 'oddly' rearranges ENOUGH plus UT.
explanation.definitionFit: Huguenots were French Protestants, many of whom fled persecution abroad.

clue.text: Football team to make comeback — nothing un-British in that

annotationWithheld.why: Football team to make comeback — nothing un-British in that (6): ORIENT is the team, but no parse of the remaining words gives the letters; the scan matches the text
annotationWithheld.clue: Football team to make comeback — nothing un-British in that

clue.text: Last word about German and the pole he discovered

indicators.note: about means placed around, so amen surrounds the rest

parts.note: amen is the last word of a prayer
und is German for and
S stands for the south pole

explanation.surface: A tale ending with a German and the polar region he reached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts UND and S inside AMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian explorer was the first to reach the South Pole, in 1911.

clue.text: Returning Number One volume, a student appears much affected

indicators.note: returning means the three pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tome is a large book or volume
L is a learner, as on a British learner-driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student is visibly moved on getting back the first volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns NOITOME into EMOTION; L is the learner plate on British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deeply moved or stirred by feeling is in this state.

clue.text: Togs including cogs?

definitions.meaning: togs is informal for clothes or kit
a toothed wheel set or mechanism with cogs

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both clothing kit and a toothed wheel mechanism.

clue.text: The moth that has crossed the asses' bridge?

definitions.meaning: a moth whose caterpillar is a looper, seeming to measure the ground

definitions.text: that has crossed the asses' bridge?
definitions.meaning: the pons asinorum is Euclid's fifth proposition, a hurdle for learners of geometry

explanation.walkthrough: The asses' bridge (pons asinorum) is a Euclid proposition that weak students fail to get past.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a moth family and a person skilled in Euclid's science.

clue.text: She causes a painter to be all upset

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman makes an artist completely upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabella is a woman's name.

clue.text: Many are making the challenge

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lots of people are taking up the gauntlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dare is a challenge to do something risky.

clue.text: Takes scornful view of French mince-pies on board

parts.note: de is the French for of

indicators.note: on board a ship means inside the letters for steamship

parts.note: SS is a steamship, a vessel one goes on board

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up, so the word pies is chopped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at French mince pies served aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' rearranges PIES as PISE; 'on' board puts it inside SS (steamship), after DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To despise is to regard with contempt or disdain.

clue.text: Ever ripe for change, or a stay of execution

indicators.note: for change means the letters are altered into another order

explanation.surface: Always ready to change, or a condemned prisoner's last-minute respite.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is a cancellation or postponement of punishment.

clue.text: Isle has small wood, just one tree

parts.note: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea
a grove is a small wood

explanation.surface: An island has a small copse of trees, but just one.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangrove is a tropical tree growing in coastal swamps.

clue.text: Roles of flamingoes in Wonderland

parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's story the Queen's croquet game uses flamingoes to strike the hedgehog balls

explanation.surface: A question about what parts the pink birds play in Carroll's story.
explanation.definitionFit: In the croquet scene, the birds stand in for the hammers used to hit the ball.

clue.text: No fixed location in Alabama?

definitions.meaning: able to move about freely, not stationary
a port city on the Gulf coast of that state

explanation.definitionFit: The word means movable, and is also a port city in Alabama.

clue.text: Sight-seers see topless burlesque performers

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the word is taken off

parts.note: strippers perform striptease in burlesque shows

explanation.surface: Tourists go to watch a risqué show.
explanation.definitionFit: Trippers are people on a day out or excursion.

clue.text: The farmer's in control of course

definitions.meaning: one who tills the soil, the 's read as is
the handle that steers a boat

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a cultivator of land and a boat's steering lever.

clue.text: Sheep pursues wolf, alias this — It's elementary

definitions.text: Sheep pursues wolf, alias this — It's elementary

parts.words: Sheep pursues wolf, alias this — It's elementary
parts.note: a ram, a male sheep, placed after wolf gives the alternative name of this chemical element

explanation.surface: A ram chases a wolf, and the explanation is simple.
explanation.walkthrough: WOLF followed by RAM gives WOLFRAM, the other name for this metal, which is an element.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten, chemical symbol W, is a metallic element also called wolfram.

clue.text: Car wrecked by Eros' dart

indicators.note: wrecked means the letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A vehicle is damaged by Cupid's arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadster is an open two-seater sports car.

clue.text: Bound to be beaten

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both tied securely and flogged.
